//: buildCommand overrides the `build` script for deploys only, and the
reason it is here rather than folded into `build` is that `prisma migrate
deploy` needs a reachable database. Putting it in `build` would make
`npm run build` — which developers run to check a change compiles — fail
on a machine with no Postgres running, and fail with P3005 on any local
database that predates prisma/migrations. Deploys are the only place the
migration must run, so it is the only place it is wired.
This is what closes the gap docs/WORKFLOW.md used to document: schema
reaches production because the deploy applies it, not because someone
Ordering matters. `migrate deploy` runs BEFORE `next build`, so a
migration that fails takes the build down and the currently deployed
version keeps serving. If it ran after, or as a post-deploy step, there
would be a window where new code that selects a new column is live
against a database that does not have it — and because Prisma selects
every scalar field, that window is not a degraded feature, it is every
buildCommand: prisma generate && prisma migrate deploy && next build
